hook.text: Replace every plank of a ship one by one. When the last plank is swapped, is it still the same ship?

buildup.text: This paradox dates to ancient Greece and challenges what makes something the same thing over time.

discovery.text: If the rebuilt ship is the same, identity survives total material change. If not, when exactly did it stop?

twist.text: Now reassemble the old planks into a second ship. Which one is the original? Both have a claim.

climax.text: The paradox reveals that identity isn't in the materials—it's in continuity, pattern, or something harder to define.

punchline.text: Every cell in your body is replaced too. Are you still you?

quiz.question: What does the Ship of Theseus challenge?
options: What makes something the same thing over time
